domain_hypothesis.reasoning: The schema contains BillingAddress, BillingCity, BillingCountry, InvoiceId, CustomerId, InvoiceDate, and Total, which are the quintessential properties of a transactional invoice database (highly resembles the Chinook music store database schema).

kpi_specs.name: Total Revenue
kpi_specs.description: The sum of all invoice totals, indicating the cumulative revenue generated across all transactions.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT SUM(Total) AS total_revenue FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: A single summary metric representing the financial performance baseline is standard for sales dashboards.

kpi_specs.name: Average Invoice Value
kpi_specs.description: The average value of a generated invoice, helping to understand customer basket size and average transaction value.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT AVG(Total) AS average_invoice_value FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: Useful metric alongside overall revenue to track changes in pricing power or product mix sales.

kpi_specs.name: Monthly Sales Performance Trend
kpi_specs.description: Monthly aggregated revenue to show trends over time, highlighting seasonal fluctuations and growth trajectory.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', InvoiceDate) AS sales_month, SUM(Total) AS monthly_revenue FROM data GROUP BY sales_month ORDER BY sales_month ASC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Line charts are ideal for depicting trends over time. Standard SQLite date formatting is applied to the InvoiceDate column.

kpi_specs.name: Revenue by Billing Country
kpi_specs.description: Aggregated sales revenue grouped by country to identify primary geographic markets.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS total_revenue FROM data GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A bar chart is best for comparing categorical groups (countries) in descending order of value.

kpi_specs.name: Top Customers by Total Spent
kpi_specs.description: Identifies the highest-value customers based on their lifetime spending history and order count.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT CustomerId, COUNT(InvoiceId) AS total_orders, SUM(Total) AS total_spend FROM data GROUP BY CustomerId ORDER BY total_spend DESC LIMIT 10
kpi_specs.reasoning: A tabular format is ideal for displaying multi-column detail, and sorting by spending highlights VIP clients.
